Summary: The DRAGIN framework, as described in the sources, is a dynamic retrieval augmented generation system that determines when to retrieve external knowledge and formulates effective queries for retrieval based on the LLM’s real-time information needs. It operates through two primary components: Real-time Information Needs Detection (RIND) and Query Formulation based on Self-attention (QFS). RIND identifies when to retrieve based on LLM internal states, while QFS leverages attention mechanisms to determine what to retrieve. The framework is designed to be lightweight and adaptable across different model architectures without requiring additional training or fine-tuning.
